ttd.basisLabel: Gross average weekly wage before taxes
ttd.rateText: Sixty-six and two-thirds percent of average weekly wages, not more than the average weekly wage in the State for the preceding fiscal year (S.C. Code § 42-9-10(A)).
ttd.minText: Not less than $75 a week, unless that exceeds the employee's average weekly salary, in which case the employee receives the full average weekly salary (§ 42-9-10(A)).
ttd.periodLabel: accidents on or after January 1, 2026 (SAWW certified by the Department of Employment and Workforce for July 1, 2024 - June 30, 2025)

waiting.text: No compensation for the first seven calendar days of disability (except medical benefits); if the injury results in disability of more than fourteen days, compensation is allowed from the date of disability (S.C. Code § 42-9-200).

ttdDuration.text: In no case may the period covered by total disability compensation exceed 500 weeks, except as provided in § 42-9-10(C) for certain permanently and totally disabled workers (S.C. Code § 42-9-10(A)).

ppd.text: Scheduled injuries are paid at 66 2/3% of the average weekly wage for a fixed number of weeks (e.g. thumb 65 weeks, index finger 40 weeks) under § 42-9-30; partial loss is paid in proportion. Partial disability not on the schedule is paid at 66 2/3% of the wage difference, up to 340 weeks from the date of injury (§ 42-9-20).

facts.text: The loss of both hands, arms, shoulders, feet, legs, hips, or vision in both eyes, or any two of these, is by statute total and permanent disability (§ 42-9-10(B)).
South Carolina's statutory minimum weekly benefit is a fixed $75, not a percentage of the state average wage (§ 42-9-10(A)).
The maximum changes every January 1; it was $1,134.43 for 2025 and $1,189.94 for 2026.
